raw_response:
I've been working this land since I was sixteen. My father grew cotton here, and his father before him. Nine mu of cotton — that's what I know, that's what I'll plant again this year.

The seeds I'll use are the improved hybrid variety — the same kind I switched to about fifteen years ago when I saw my neighbor's yield jump up. I'm not going back to the old seeds. The hybrid gives more bolls and handles the heat better.

Before planting I'll plough deep, like I always do. Break up the hardpan, mix in the base fertilizer. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, then top-dress with urea twice — once when the buds set, once when the bolls are forming. That's what my fields need here in Quzhou. The soil tells me.

For water, I have my well. I'll water before I plant to get good moisture in the ground. Then again at bud stage, flowering, boll fill, and if August is dry like last year, one more time. That's usually five times total.

Cotton is a lot of work with pests. Aphids come early, then bollworm is the real fight all through summer. I spray about eight times — I watch the plants and add more if I see damage. I've lost crops before when I didn't spray enough. Not again.

I expect around 280 jin per mu of seed cotton — a good year gives me more, a hot dry August gives me less.
